clue.text: On the way, widespread conflict

parts.note: ST, the abbreviation for street, a common crossword stand-in for a way or road
rife means prevalent, found everywhere

explanation.surface: A traveller notices that quarrelling has broken out everywhere along the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is bitter disagreement or fighting, a close synonym of conflict.

clue.text: Spill liquid over prominent display

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to splatter water or another fluid on something
second meaning: a big showy feature

explanation.definitionFit: Splash is both a verb for spattering fluid and a noun for an eye-catching headline or show.

clue.text: Regularly goes improperly into this police collection?

indicators.note: improperly means in the wrong way, so the letters of the two words are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A habitual offender keeps ending up among the police's file of mugshots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' tempts you to take alternate letters, but the whole word is anagram fodder; the surface also hints at the rogues who belong in the collection.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogues' gallery is a police file of photographs of known offenders.

clue.text: Soft soap for washing cloth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: flattering or evasive talk
second meaning: a small square of towelling used to wash the face

explanation.surface: A gentle soap is recommended for laundering a piece of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a flannel is a face cloth, and flannel is also smooth, evasive talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Flannel means flattering or wordy talk, and a flannel is a face cloth used when washing.

clue.text: One demonstrating how to get clean

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ..., someone who shows something
second meaning: a spray of water you stand under to wash

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word as SHOW-ER, one who shows; the second is the bathroom fixture, pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing under a spray of water is an everyday method of washing, while someone who exhibits things is literally one who shows.

clue.text: Large bird man much admired at back of barn

parts.note: a hero is a man people look up to

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word barn

explanation.surface: A great bird, much loved by the farmer, roosts at the rear of the barn.
explanation.definitionFit: The heron is a tall long-legged wading bird of rivers and marshes.

clue.text: Lost in reverie, doing the shearing?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: literally collecting fleece, as shearers do

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: gathering wool from sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolgathering is idle daydreaming, while taken literally it is collecting fleece.

clue.text: Snake's warning is to disconcert

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the rattlesnake's buzzing tail
second meaning: to unsettle or fluster someone

explanation.surface: The hiss or buzz of a snake is meant to unnerve whoever is near.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattlesnake shakes its tail as an alarm, and to rattle someone is to unsettle them.

clue.text: Haul half a gallon back in trailer

indicators.note: read backwards, so the haul and the half-gallon are turned round together

parts.note: to haul is to drag

indicators.note: only the first half of the word is kept

explanation.surface: Someone tows a container of fuel back in a trailer behind the car.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'trailer' a towed vehicle, but here it is the definition: a person who trails behind the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard lags behind the rest, so a trailer in the sense of a straggler.

clue.text: One working on hard stuff prepared drill site

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so these letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A construction worker deals with tough rock at a drilling site that has been got ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard stuff' suggests rock or concrete; it is slang for spirits such as whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A distiller makes spirits, and the hard stuff is a colloquial term for strong liquor.

clue.text: For the night, settle son in base

indicators.note: in places the letter for son inside the word for base

parts.note: the root of something is its base or foundation

explanation.surface: A parent arranges for their boy to bed down at a camp or base overnight.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds roost when they perch and settle down to sleep at night.

clue.text: Rear small bird

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear' looks like a verb about raising a young bird; it is the noun for the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the back part of a boat, so it is the rear end.

clue.text: Gales rage round north-eastern part of Africa

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters go around the compass abbreviation
gales that rage are thrown about wildly, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word taken as written, its letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Storms blow fiercely around the north-east corner of the African continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The country is in West Africa, not the north-east; 'north-eastern' is just the two letters NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a nation on the Atlantic coast of West Africa, so a part of that continent.

clue.text: Good holiday home rejected, perhaps worker is to travel for pleasure

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the holiday home word is read in reverse

parts.note: a villa is a house rented for a holiday
a worker is one kind of ant, so ant is an example

explanation.surface: Turning down a holiday villa, a working person decides to roam for fun instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallivant is to go about gadding from place to place in search of amusement.

clue.text: In danger, like a condemned heretic?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: at risk, in jeopardy
second meaning: literally tied to the post to be burned

explanation.walkthrough: Heretics were once burned tied to a wooden post, so the phrase is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at risk is in jeopardy, while a heretic sentenced to burning was tied to a post.

clue.text: Chaos regularly over benefits for accommodation

indicators.note: over puts the picked letters above the next word in this down entry
regularly picks every other letter of the word chaos

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of the word chaos
uses are benefits or advantages

explanation.surface: Turmoil in the benefits system leaves people without anywhere to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Houses are dwellings, so they provide places to live, which is accommodation.

clue.text: Hole in ground, and box on right

indicators.note: on puts the box word above the letter for right in this down entry

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box for goods

explanation.surface: A pit has been dug, with a packing case lying on its right-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a bowl-shaped hollow in the ground, made by a meteor, bomb or volcano.

clue.text: A gusher, Leo, will broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Leo, an effusive talker, is going to make an announcement on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A gusher' reads as a gushing person; here it is a well spouting petroleum.
explanation.definitionFit: A gusher is a well from which crude petroleum spurts out under its own pressure.

clue.text: Defeated, beheaded — and polished off by cannibal?

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter of the word for defeated is cut off

parts.note: to be beaten is to be defeated

explanation.surface: A vanquished enemy loses his head and ends up as a cannibal's dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Food polished off by a cannibal has been consumed, and the question mark flags the grisly example.

clue.text: Possibly libellous remark needs attention on returned manuscript

indicators.note: on places the word for attention after the reversed abbreviation
returned means the abbreviation for manuscript is sent back the other way

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay them attention

explanation.surface: An editor flags a defamatory comment in a manuscript that has come back for review.
explanation.definitionFit: A smear is a damaging and often false accusation, the kind of statement that can be libellous.

clue.text: Exhausted, having done this shopping?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tired out or used up
second meaning: past tense of spend, what you have done with money at the shops

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a shopping trip leaves both the shopper and the wallet worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent describes someone completely drained of energy and money that has been paid out.

clue.text: Practical person concerned with an agenda

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
the indefinite article an has the same sense as a
an agenda is a list of items to be discussed

explanation.surface: A pragmatic committee member only cares about what is on the meeting's agenda.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist deals with things as they actually are, a sensible, down-to-earth sort.

clue.text: Pronouncing a proverb

definitions.meaning: first meaning: uttering or speaking words
second meaning: a well-known maxim or adage

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the present participle of the verb to say and a noun for a familiar adage.

clue.text: I cadge one small breakfast in pub

indicators.note: in puts the breakfast item inside the word for pub

parts.note: a bar is a drinking place
a single egg makes a small breakfast

explanation.surface: Someone admits to scrounging a boiled egg in a pub for their morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer: a person who cadges would describe themselves this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A beggar is someone who asks others for money or food, which is cadging.
